Summarize a choice model

Source: R/methods.R
summary.choicemodel.Rd

Summarize a choice model

Usage

# S3 method for class 'choicemodel'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

object

A "choicemodel" fit.

...

Unused.

Value

An object of class "summary.choicemodel" with the coefficient table (coefficients: estimate, standard error, z, p), the parameter block of every row ("outcome", "generic", "fixed effect", "inflation", "nest", "scale", "covariance", "random intercept"), and the fit statistics. The z statistics of the inclusive-value and scale blocks test the value 1 (the multinomial logit); those of the multinomial probit covariance block test the values under independent, identically distributed errors (variances 1, covariances 0.5 under the normalization of the first variance to 1); the random-intercept standard deviations get no z test (their null is on the boundary); a parameter whose variance is negative (the Hessian is not positive definite) has standard error NA. The printed table of a penalized fit (firth = TRUE or a prior) marks [sep] the coefficients that move along a separating direction of the data (separation()). Their Wald tests rest on a quadratic approximation of the penalized log-likelihood that fails along that direction and can be far off (Heinze and Schemper 2002); under a prior they can have little power (Rainey 2024). Test them by term_test(type = "lr") or lr_test(). A maximum-likelihood fit names its diverging coefficients in a warning at fit time instead.

See also

fit_stats() for the pseudo-R-squared measures.
